FINDINGS.finding: The recovery fail-closed defect from the previous independent review is corrected at c74edc491e4520f686cc1604bb8141bf177b4f92. recovery() now derives mid only when identity is a dict, requires name(mid) before dictionary membership, returns SAFE_BLOCK for malformed/unattributable authority and appends a canonical SAFE_BLOCK audit event only when a valid string mission_id identifies an existing nonterminal mission.

Focused recovery regression now covers identity=None, string/list/empty dict, unhashable list/dict mission_id, null/unknown mission_id, wrong-shape attributable identity, non-dict snapshot and non-dict observation. Unattributable malformed inputs return the exact SAFE_BLOCK result with byte-identical journal state; attributable malformed inputs append exactly one canonical recovery_decision.

The earlier one-use retry correction also remains intact: an authorization occupies the retry slot through claim and restore, no second authorization is possible before the claimed next attempt is bound, binding consumes that used slot, and a new ticket becomes possible only after the newly bound latest attempt subsequently fails or becomes uncertain.

M3 action_receipt still does not implement the PLAN's bounded receipt schema for action_id. The branch calls imported checked_receipt() and then stores the receipt, but checked_receipt validates only exact keys, status, result_sha256 and bounded summary; it imposes no type, format or length constraint on action_id. Consequently an action_id may be a boolean, list, object or arbitrarily large string and still be durably accepted. This violates the independently reread M3 PLAN requirement for a bounded synthetic action-receipt schema.

Importing the M1 helper does not provide the missing M3 protection. In M1, action_id is separately required to equal the deterministic canonical SHA-256 action identity before a receipt is accepted. M3 has no corresponding equality or format check, so the helper alone is insufficient. The existing M3 valid fixture happens to use a 64-hex action_id but no implementation invariant enforces that representation.

The action-receipt tests cover exact duplicate idempotency and a conflicting status, but do not reject malformed or unbounded action_id values and do not prove replay rejects a recomputed hash-chain/head containing such a receipt. This leaves a concrete required bounded-schema/replay conformance gap.

The retained Fresh runtime files are byte-identical to the previously reviewed fc8c3be1b648c978d6beda02dc4586b21453ad92 versions; the fix1 implementation delta contains no Fresh source modification. The bounded inspect_draft metadata, composer re-resolution, Host/Origin/token/component readiness checks and exact tab/URL reply gates therefore remain unchanged.

The retained Fresh evidence remains deliberately limited. fresh_protocol.md still records the observed first-send uncertainty: the native tab navigated to a new thread but no binding/result reached the controller before timeout and no retry send was written. Nothing in fix1 converts that observation into a successful first-send or production-readiness claim.

The integration limitations are still explicit: cross_repository_scope is UNMEASURED, M3 documentation leaves multi-repository and OS-reboot behavior unmeasured, and the bounded two-worktree Chrome evidence is not a full-browser or general production qualification.

All twelve independently fetched files listed by m3/fix1/source_hashes.json match their declared Git blob IDs. d3e1ae5ea38fc8957175930381ca9b1af72a6748 -> c74edc491e4520f686cc1604bb8141bf177b4f92 is one bounded correction commit touching only M3 source/docs/tests plus prior-review evidence; c74edc491e4520f686cc1604bb8141bf177b4f92 -> 549b8f7b58c2387f89881bc303124f5d1421a5f4 is one evidence-only commit. Reported gates are 193 Python passes, 181 Node passes, 27 syntax files, manifest PASS and diff PASS.

REVIEW_SUMMARY: The exact incoming authority 549b8f7b58c2387f89881bc303124f5d1421a5f4, every required incoming path and every required immutable ref were independently read through the official GitHub connector. The iteration-3 recovery input-boundary defect is genuinely fixed, with substantive malformed-authority regressions, and the prior one-use retry correction remains sound. Retained Fresh runtime blobs are unchanged and continue to preserve their bounded diagnostic/auth/readiness/reply contracts and explicit first-send uncertainty. One separate substantive M3 PLAN defect remains: action_receipt is described as a bounded synthetic receipt but M3 never validates action_id at all; unlike M1, there is no canonical-action equality check to supply that constraint. Malformed or arbitrarily large action_id values can therefore enter the sealed M3 journal, and current tests do not cover public or replay rejection. M3 cannot close until that bounded receipt invariant is enforced.
